elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..." — the take-or-pay USD 2,000,000/year three-year obligation is excised, and §12.3 independently records Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. No retained shortfall, instalment or contingent payment mechanic remains.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2.1: "...and will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term." This is consistent with retained §7.1 (Fees stated in each Order Form; no unidentified minimum-use charge), so payment is tied to usage or ordered Services only.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the rendered §2.1 leaves no purchase or volume commitment of any kind, so there is no commitment to limit to a 12-month term. The preferred outcome subsumes this fallback constraint.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no minimum commitment remaining in §2.1 (and §12.3 confirming none exists), there is nothing to reduce; a reduction right is unnecessary and its absence does not leave Customer bound to any volume.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the take-or-pay basis and its shortfall exposure were deleted entirely, so no shortfall can arise and no penalty formula or contingent payment mechanic is retained anywhere in §2.1 or §7.1.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: rendered §2.1 states both that Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment and that Customer pays only for Services used or ordered, matching the two preferred elements in operative language rather than only in the comment.

The walk-away feature (multi-year take-or-pay, USD 2,000,000/year for three years, expressly 'without reduction or termination rights') is removed unconditionally, with no residual shortfall, instalment or penalty mechanic left behind.

Minimality holds: only §2.1 was rewritten. §7.1 and §12.3 are reproduced verbatim with no cosmetic deletions or paraphrase, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories, expense language) were added.

Intent preserved: the replacement leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference — Fees, Order Form and Services remain as defined, §7.1's Order-Form-based fee mechanic and its bar on unidentified minimum-use charges still operate, and §12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement is now consistent rather than contradicted.

Termination/exit rights are deliberately not addressed here, correctly avoiding duplication with T4C; the fallback is offered in the margin comment only, which is appropriate since the operative text achieves the preferred position.
